options.text: Every string that begins with 'Hello, ' followed by any string

questions.explanation: A template literal type matches strings following the pattern — here, anything starting with 'Hello, '.
Unions in a template expand to every combination — the cross product of the two unions.

questions.prompt: Which are the intrinsic string-manipulation types? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The intrinsics are Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize, and Uncapitalize. There is no built-in Reverse.

questions.prompt: How do template literal types help mapped types?

options.text: In key remapping (as), they generate new key names like `on${Capitalize<K>}`

questions.explanation: Template literal types build new key names in a mapped type's as clause, e.g. turning click into onClick.

questions.prompt: To extract the part of a string type before a dot, use template ______ in a conditional: S extends `${infer P}.${string}` ? P : never. (one word)
questions.explanation: Template literal patterns can use infer to capture substrings, enabling type-level parsing of structured strings.

questions.prompt: Do intrinsic string types like `Uppercase<T>` work on runtime string values?

options.text: No — they operate on string types only; use String.prototype methods for runtime values

questions.explanation: The intrinsics transform string types at compile time. To uppercase a value at runtime, use String.prototype.toUpperCase.
